ONTARIO CAMPS ASSOCIATION FONDS, TRENT UNIVERSITY ARCHIVES, 72-007 — FINDING AID
================================================================================
Fetched raw and stripped of markup 2026-09-06 from https://archives.trentu.ca/index.php/72-007
Donated by the OCA Archives Committee, 1971. Two series: Camp Brochures and Photographs (1922-1967),
and Organizational Records (1952-1973).

NOTE ON THE AUDIO: "The audio tapes have been physically removed from this fonds and been placed
within a new fonds titled Canadian Camping Association fonds : Sound Tape Recordings (83-002)."
Associated: 77-024 (L. M. Frost fonds), 80-022 (M. L. Northway fonds).

Northway), n.d. Temagami Ned, 1909, b/w, 9 x 14 1/2, no neg. Folder 7: Abundance of Beautiful Trees at Camp Tonakela, Madras, India. Half the value of the camp to girls and boys from treeless areas of Madras City lies in its fifteen acres of lovely green trees. Except for some tall palms on the fringes it was a barren waste in 1946. Every tree shown here was planted since then by the staff and committee members. b/w, 21 1/2 x 16, no neg. Box 6 Folder 17: Centenary Journey Good camping means experience and skill in building fireplaces and fires, as well as knowing how to cook and erect pot holders. At Centenary Journey participants must be well versed in camping skills prior to taking a Trip. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. Mountains, as well as rivers and lakes must be crossed on the Voyageurs Highway. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. "Getting there is half the fun" - and half the fun is portaging past white water, dangerous rapids, dams and other man-made obstacles. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. A highlight of any trip is the meals... especially when a group experiments with Bannock (Balsam Portage, Saskatchewan). b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. Good trippers must also be experienced in the art of map reading and compass work. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. A good tripper takes time out to relax, explore, and fish (Sturgeon Weir River, Saskatchewan - a group from the Regina YMCA). b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. A stark reminder of a man-made Lake. Once a small stream winding through beautiful countryside the naked trees are epitaphs to the advances of the lumbering and hydro industries. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. Sleeping under the stars will be a wonderful part of Centenary Journey. But good campers must always be prepared for rain. Tents must be properly pitched and trenched. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. Grand Portage - a key centre in the early commerce of Canada. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. On Mirond Lake, Saskatchewan, a group of Centenary Journey participants from the Regina YMCA Camp take time to pose for a photograph which will go in many scrapbooks - a pleasant reminder of the part they played in the Camping Associations' Centennial Project. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. To participate campers must also know how to handle a canoe in White Water. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. Other campers look on enviously as a group sets off on their trip (Mahood Lake, British Columbia). b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. Exploration and research will be an important part of the responsibilities of Centenary Journey participants. On side trips troops will enjoy discovering old Indian cabins, and taking the time to meet local inhabitants who can spend hours around a campfire relating legends of the past. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. And so the day begins! - Or is it the end of a portage? In any event from land to water brings on new thrills and anticipation of what lies beyond. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg. Indian villages and reservations still lie along the Voyageurs Highway. Canoeists welcome the opportunity to find such a village and visit with its inhabitants. b/w, 25 1/2 x 20, no neg.
